findings.where: the ruled stock behind 'stool and le...', 'they will bri...', 'no name on...' — the crop the rubric says to judge at three hundred per cent
findings.what: The printed rules cut through the middle of the writing instead of sitting under it: in the crop the rules lie at y=239, 482 and 722 (pitch 242 crop px = 80.7 px of the still) and the inked bands run 174-344, 414-593 and 702-779, so each rule crosses its line of writing 38%, 38% and 26% of the way down the letters; measured back on the full still the same note has an 81.0 px rule pitch against a ~36 px written-line pitch, 2.25 written lines per printed rule, and evidence/logs/lines.json records the same thing for the whole set at a median 0.373 of the pitch off the nearest rule where laid out with no relation at all reads 0.25.
findings.why: The row is 'the paper reads as photographed rather than simulated', and writing that runs through the ruling of the sheet it is on is the single clearest tell that the sheet is a picture behind a text layer rather than a sheet somebody wrote on — it is the first thing visible at the magnification the row names, and lines.json says in the evidence that nothing gates it.

findings.where: the handwritten notes — the header note at y 37-257 and the 'somebody has taken the tall stool' note at y 1961-2417
findings.what: Repeated letters are pixel-identical. Cross-correlating every pair of same-size ink components at native scale (no rescaling), 27 of 339 marks in the frame (8.0%) have a twin at ncc >= 0.98 and 68 (20.1%) at >= 0.95; inside the one note the crops come from it is 16 of 114 (14.0%) at >= 0.98 and 45 (39.5%) at >= 0.95, with six pairs over 0.99 — two 'e' at 0.9933, two 'o' at 0.9897, two 'd' at 0.9880, two 'a' at 0.9873. Inside crops/02_chat_300_hand.png itself the closest pair reads 0.9802. evidence/logs/fonts.json gives the reason: the hands carry five variants per glyph and a measured same-variant rate of 0.3006, so on a screen this dense identical twins are arithmetically unavoidable.
findings.why: 'Handwriting whose repeated letters are identical' is named verbatim in what this row is looking for, and evidence/logs/hand.json reports twin_share 0.0 at IoU 0.99 — a normalised-box overlap is more forgiving than a reader's eye at three hundred per cent, which is where the row is judged.

findings.where: the desk immediately beside every sheet
findings.what: The contact shadow does not survive the second lighting condition and is missing from two daylight stills. Measured as a paired comparison on rays that stay on desk for 46 px — the desk 8-20 px out from a sheet's edge against the same rays 30-44 px out — the daylight stills give a consistent upper-left key: median darkening below a sheet of +8.4 (02_chat), +13.7 (03_us), +14.6 (05_settings), +21.2 (13_messenger_states), with the up side at -1.6 to -4.3. In crops/dusk_pulse.png every side is flat or reversed: down -0.56, up -2.87, right -3.76, left -0.95 (medians). In 12_search the down side reads +0.06 (mean) and in 01_pulse -4.06, i.e. no shadow at all. evidence/logs/holes.json reports 'darker_by' of 17.83 for 01_pulse and 18.43 for 12_search, which I could not reproduce from the pixels with any near/far band I tried.
findings.why: The row asks for 'contact shadows baked from the render's own lighting rather than applied as a uniform blur'. A shadow that vanishes when the scene is re-lit, and that is absent under two of the ten daylight heroes, is not coming from the render's lighting.

findings.artifact: 01_pulse.png, confirmed at larger scale in crops/reception_picked_up.png
findings.where: the feelings row, the 'confetti' object at 16:23 and its neighbours
findings.what: Two of the six confetti pieces are flat vector fills and none of the feeling objects casts a contact shadow. The chip at (590,1281), 33x29 px, has an interior luma sd of 0.85 with 23 distinct RGB triples over 342 pixels, and the chip at (507,1300), 27x24 px, reads sd 0.89 with 29 triples over 126 pixels — beside chips in the same object that read sd 19.3 and 21.1 with 50 and 209 triples and visible tooth. Under each object, desk 2-16 px below against 34-54 px below: the paper scrap 'empty chair' darkens by +8.81 grey levels, 'hold' by +2.49, 'nyeh' by -0.16 and the confetti cluster by -6.67. evidence/logs/surfaces.json files obj_confetti under 'read_but_not_measurable' ('only 1 whole blocks of this surface') and evidence/logs/flat.json cannot see a 33 px chip at all — its window is 80 px.
findings.why: 'Feelings as physical objects rather than icons' is one of the row's own criteria, and a flat pastel lozenge lying on a desk with no shadow under it is an icon; the objects and the paper beside them also disagree about where the light is.

findings.where: the Moments grid, and the video open in the media viewer
findings.what: The couple's photographs and video are untextured renders. Across five Moments tiles the mean chroma (max minus min channel) is 3.47 to 8.60 out of 255, with 37% to 85% of pixels under 6 — grey spheres and boxes on grey backdrops under a hard key. In 14_media_viewer the 'sea' holds 98 distinct RGB triples in an 80,000 px patch of sky (0.1%) and 556 in the 366,903 px region evidence/logs/flat.json names as its largest flat area, against 4.4% distinct triples for the desk and 6.1% for clean paper measured in 02_chat by the same code.
findings.why: In a row about whether surfaces read as photographed rather than simulated, the surfaces that are supposed to be actual photographs are the most obviously synthetic thing in the set, and flat.json defends them as 'what a photograph of a sky actually is' when the banding count says they are a rendered gradient.

findings.artifact: 10_first_run.png (and the desk in every other frame)
findings.where: the large empty desk between the header note and the single message, (120,600)-(1320,1200)
findings.what: The desk carries almost no fine detail. High-pass standard deviation at sigma=1 is 1.49 grey levels against 12.78 at sigma=16, a ratio of 0.116; clean paper in the same set reads 0.299 to 0.405 by the same measure and the rendered sky in 14_media_viewer reads 0.105. Autocorrelation of the desk finds no tile (best peak past the central lobe 0.21), so it is not repeating — it is soft vertical stripes with no pores, rays or checks. evidence/logs/grain.json passes it on fine_detail_share 1.83 against a floor of 1.60, a 14% margin, and its own note concedes that its anisotropy term 'cannot see the difference between painted stripes and visible oak'.
findings.why: The desk is the largest surface in every one of the seventeen artifacts; if it reads as painted the whole scene reads as an illustration of a desk with paper on it, and the only check in the evidence that looks at it says it cannot tell the difference.

findings.what: Ten of the seventeen region reports record sheets drawn with no paper on them at the moment the picture was taken — sticky_blue_02 x2 in eight of them, sticky_blue_02 x2 plus graph_03 x1 in 12_search, sticky_blue_02_dusk x3 in dusk_pulse — which by the build's own description means those pieces painted the flat fallback colour under them. Nothing in the evidence shows where they are: I searched all ten stills plus dusk_pulse for connected regions of 1500 px or more whose 9x9 local standard deviation is under 0.35 and found none, and evidence/logs/flat.json agrees (files_with_a_flat_fill: 0, sheets_with_no_paper_on_them empty for every still).
findings.why: A sheet painted as a flat fill is the anti-goal verbatim, the record says it happened in more than half the set, and no picture or check in the evidence locates a single one — so a reader cannot tell whether the anti-goal was tripped on screen or the sheets were off it.

findings.what: The file contradicts its own table. Its per-still pitches run 70.5 px (01_pulse) to 599.0 px (04_moments) and the file computes ratio: 8.5, then says three lines later 'It is 1.86 now'; BRIEFING.md describes the same file as '61 to 178 pixels ... a ratio of 2.9'. My own measurement — autocorrelating the blue-channel row profile over ink-free columns — gives 81 px for 02_chat (the file says 161.0), 88 px for 01_pulse (70.5) and 113 px for 05_settings (106.5).
findings.why: The rule pitch is the only number in the evidence that says at what physical scale the stock is being drawn, and three different values for it appear in two files that are supposed to describe the same measurement.

what_is_working: No tear repeats on any single screen, checked both ways. The app's own reports give distinct tear ids for every row in every scene that records them (5/5 in 02_chat, 7/7 in 13_messenger_states, 6/6 in 08_state_propagating, 5/5 in 12_search, 4/4 in 11_chat_scroll and 14_media_viewer); cross-correlating all twelve tear silhouettes I extracted from 02_chat myself, the worst pair reads |xcorr| 0.465 at lag 118, which is not a repeat.

The tear edges themselves hold up at three hundred per cent. Silhouette roughness at the visible boundary (first pixel over luma 150, high-passed over 31 samples) runs 1.33 to 9.96 px rms across the eight edges I measured in 02_chat, inside the band evidence/logs/torn.json says a reader was content with, and in crops/02_chat_300_shadow.png the fringe is individual strands with gaps between them rather than a serrated stamp. torn.json's generator profile self-correlates at most 0.339 past its central lobe against 0.804-0.811 for the two-sine shape it replaced, measured as a control in the same file.

No tiled repeating texture and no screen-fixed noise overlay, which are two of the three things that would put this row under its floor outright. Desk autocorrelation peaks at 0.21 past the central lobe in 01_pulse and 0.024 in 02_chat. Across 203 detrended 64x64 clean-paper windows in four stills, the worst within-frame pair reads |ncc| 0.126 (02_chat), 0.161 (17_setup_pwa), 0.111 (03_us), 0.096 (12_search). In 11_chat_scroll the paper texture correlates with the note it travelled with (0.466 and 0.382 at the frame's 234 px shift) and never with the screen position it left (-0.015, 0.008).

The fold in 06_unfolding is rendered geometry catching light, not a flat image being transformed. Stepping the 142-frame sequence in app time (16 ms a frame, playback_over_app_time 1.0), the folded panel's luma sweeps smoothly 149 -> 159 -> 179 -> 201 -> 213 -> 223 -> 237 over frames 13-67 and back down 221 -> 203 -> 179 on the second fold, an 88-level swing, with the panel body flat to +/-1.5 levels as a single directional light would leave it and the crease dropping to 162 at the fold. The landed note casts a real shadow: the desk under it reads 55-60 against 90 beside it, a 35-level drop with a 20 px penumbra, lying down and to the right — the same direction as the stills' contact shadows.

Pressure variance in the ink is real and measurable on the glass, not just in the font file. On 02_chat's big note the stroke width from a distance transform has cv 0.504 (p5 2.0 px, p50 4.0, p95 6.0 at three times scale) and the ink core luma along the ridge runs p5 53.6 to p95 125.9 with sd 22.0 over 3,408 samples — not a constant-weight fill.

The library behind it is deep rather than a few assets reused: 54 paper surfaces (27 day, 27 dusk) and 62 object surfaces measured in evidence/logs/surfaces.json, 56 tear masks and 49 cut edges in torn.json, three hands in fonts.json, and a fully re-lit second condition in crops/dusk_pulse.png with its own dusk stocks.
verdict: The expensive half of this is genuinely there: no tear repeats on any screen by either the app's record or my own cross-correlation of the silhouettes, no tile and no screen-fixed noise field anywhere I could find it, a fold sequence whose panels sweep 88 grey levels as they rotate under one light and cast a real 35-level shadow when they land, and ink whose stroke width varies by half its mean. None of the three things that would sink this row outright — procedural noise overlay, tiled texture, beige rectangle — is visible in the pixels. What keeps it under 22 is what happens at the exact magnification the row names. In crops/02_chat_300_hand.png the printed rules cross the writing 26-38% of the way down the letters, at a pitch of 80.7 px against a written-line pitch near 36 — that is the finding holding this row at its floor, because a sheet whose ruling has no relation to what is written on it reads as a photograph with text composited over it, which is exactly what this row is asked to detect, and evidence/logs/lines.json says in the evidence that nothing gates it. Beside it, 8.0% of the ink marks in the same frame have a pixel-identical twin (14.0% inside the note the crops come from), the contact shadow that is consistent and directional in daylight goes to a median of -0.56 in the dusk condition and to zero in 12_search, two confetti chips are flat pastel fills at sd 0.85 and 0.89, the Moments photographs are grey clay renders at 3.5-8.6 chroma, the desk carries a fine-detail-to-coarse ratio of 0.116 against 0.30-0.41 for the paper on it, and ten of the seventeen reports say sheets were on the glass with no paper on them while no picture in the set shows one. The material work is real; the layer that sits on top of it — writing, glyph variety, the second light — has not caught up with it.
opened: evidence/BRIEFING.md is not an artifact; read as instructed
not_worth_opening: evidence/SCORE.json and evidence/critics/13/ — another reader's conclusions, closed as BRIEFING.md instructs.

evidence/DIFF.json, evidence/reliability.json, evidence/coldstart.json, evidence/.previous/ — these compare this capture to the last one and record how reliably it ran. Whether a surface reads as photographed is a question about this capture's pixels, and a diff against an older build cannot answer it; MANIFEST.json already told me every artifact I judged was written by this run.

evidence/logs/apk.json, pwa.json, webpush.txt, manifest.json, tests.log, strings.json — packaging, push, string and test records. Nothing in them is a surface, a light or a mark of ink. (I opened strings.json's neighbours only to confirm that; the anti-goal about product-marketing voice is another row's.)

evidence/logs/haptics.json and haptics.check.json — vibration patterns. I opened crops/haptics_strip.png because last cycle nobody did, and it is a bar chart of 36 patterns on one 2700 ms scale, with no rendered surface in it; the numeric logs behind it cannot bear on material truth.

evidence/logs/scroll_webkit.json and 11_chat_scroll.fling.json — per-frame build and raster cost, and how far the simulation asked the thread to move. That is the motion row's evidence; I used the clip's own frames instead, to ask whether the paper texture travels with the note.

evidence/logs/reception_scene.json and crops/reception_allowed.png, reception_open.png, reception_replaced.png, reception_state.png — the record says these are a desktop Chrome notification scene and not one of the seventeen artifacts. I opened reception.png and reception_picked_up.png to confirm that and because the latter is the app's own surfaces at 400 points, which I used; the rest are browser chrome.

evidence/logs/*.json scene logs other than the .report.json pairs (01_pulse.json, 02_chat.json and so on) — these are the per-step capture traces. The .report.json half carries what the app saw of its own paper, tears, stocks and masks, which is the half that bears on this row; the step traces are wall-clock harness cost, which BRIEFING.md says says nothing about the app.
evidence/experiments/ — not named in BRIEFING.md as part of the evidence set and not one of the seventeen artifacts.
